findings.problem: Compression introduced seven concrete factual, chronological, and attribution errors that were absent from the accepted expansive study and contradict the verified primary witnesses: (1) sections/12-concise-themes.tex:21 credits both William Durandus (Rationale VI.2) and John Beleth (Summa LXIV) with Durandus's verbatim Latin 'partim exultationis, et partim moeroris' and Durandus's explanation 'reserving the Christmas hymn for Christmas night', whereas Beleth (lxiv-omitted) writes 'partim laetitiae' and explains the omission of Gloria (with Ite, missa est) by eager expectation of Nativity and Resurrection; (2) sections/13-concise-commentary.tex:9 calls Gregory Hom. 1.2's six angelic choirs ('angels, archangels, thrones, dominations, principalities, and powers') 'the same angelic orders joined in the Trinity Preface', whereas the 1962 Trinity Preface (n. 1082) names four orders ('angels, archangels, cherubim, and seraphim'), omitting thrones, dominations, principalities, and powers while Gregory omits cherubim and seraphim; (3) sections/13-concise-commentary.tex:13 writes 'Ambrose departs from Gregory's judicial awe', reversing chronology by two centuries (Ambrose d. 397; Gregory d. 604); (4) sections/13-concise-commentary.tex:60 places 'at St. Mary Major' before John Beleth (Summa LV, PL 202, col. 62), implying Beleth locates his Introit remark at St. Mary Major when only Bl. Ildefonso Schuster (I, p. 321) does; (5) sections/13-concise-commentary.tex:75 cites '(Durandus VI.2, fol. 256r; Rupert III.2, PL 170, col. 58)' for 'while silent Gloria awaits Christmas night', whereas Rupert III.2 (iii.2-gloria) says silent Gloria signifies the age awaiting the joy of peace and our present waiting for the consummation of salvation, not waiting for Christmas night; (6) sections/13-concise-commentary.tex:84 (comparisontable, row 'Rom. 13:11--14a', column 'Incarnational & Marian') lists 'Christmas wake-up cry (Augustine, Sermo 185.1)', mislocating a sermon that expounds Ps. 84:12 and quotes Eph. 5:14 rather than Rom. 13:11--14a; and (7) sections/13-concise-commentary.tex:88 folds 'and the altar' into 'Christ's threefold coming (triplex adventus, Beleth Summa LXIV; Bernard In Adventu 3.3--4, 5.1) in flesh through Mary, daily in grace and the altar, and openly in majesty', erasing the accepted expansive study's boundary (sections/07-comparison.tex:17) between Beleth/Bernard's spiritual/mental advent and Schuster's Eucharistic exposition.
findings.required_result: Correct all seven passages against the verified witnesses and accepted expansive study: (1) in 12:21 separate Durandus's 'partim exultationis, et partim moeroris' and Christmas-night reservation from Beleth's 'partim laetitiae' (or attribute those exact words to Durandus alone); (2) in 13:9 state that the Trinity Preface joins the congregation to angels, archangels, cherubim, and seraphim rather than calling Gregory's six choirs 'the same angelic orders'; (3) in 13:13 replace 'Ambrose departs from Gregory's judicial awe' with non-anachronistic wording (e.g., 'In contrast to Gregory's judicial awe, Ambrose...'); (4) in 13:60 attach 'at St. Mary Major' strictly to Schuster (or the 1962 Mass), not to Beleth; (5) in 13:75 attribute awaiting Christmas night to Durandus VI.2 (fol. 256r) alone and state Rupert III.2's actual reason (or cite Rupert separately); (6) in 13:84 remove Sermo 185.1 from the Rom. 13:11--14a row or move it to the Ps. 84 row where Ps. 84:12 belongs (identifying Eph. 5:14 if the wake-up cry is kept); and (7) in 13:88 keep Beleth and Bernard's middle coming in grace distinct from the third interpretation's link to Schuster's Eucharistic altar prayers.

findings.problem: The Page 1 Four-Sense Overview bundles multiple authors behind composite clauses whose individual parts those authors do not hold, violating guidance/liturgy/propers-three-documents.md ('Where an opening, overview or summary names a reading's authors beside its thesis, credit each only with the clause he states'). In line 6 (Allegorical), '(Ambrose, Bellarmine, Augustine, Bernard, Sicard)' follows 'the incarnate Son as salutare and Fruit in Mary's "light cloud" while all nations blossom', crediting Bellarmine, Augustine, Bernard, and Sicard with Ambrose's Marian cloud and blossoming nations and crediting Ambrose with Ps. 84 salutare and Fruit; in the same line, '(Augustine, Ambrose, Bernard, Schuster)' follows 'the whole Christ (totus Christus) coming in grace and Eucharist', blurring Augustine's totus Christus, Ambrose's in singulis, Bernard's Middle Coming, and Schuster's Eucharistic exposition into one undifferentiated attribution. Similarly, line 7 (Moral) bundles '(Gregory, Bellarmine, Leo)' behind 'Detachment from worldly briers and Advent fasting, prayer, and alms' and '(Augustine, Aquinas)' behind four clauses of which only 'advancing from commandments (viae) to counsels (semitae)' belongs to Aquinas.
findings.required_result: Rewrite lines 6 and 7 of sections/11-concise-overview.tex on the model already used in line 8 (Anagogical), attaching each named author solely to the specific clause he teaches (or omitting bundled author lists from synthesis clauses) while keeping the four-row overview concise enough to stay on physical page 1.

findings.problem: A recurring register pattern of semicolon-chained one-line author verdicts and overloaded multi-argument sentences (50 to 109 words) runs throughout sections/12-concise-themes.tex and sections/13-concise-commentary.tex, violating guidance/liturgy/propers-three-documents.md ('keep one argument to a sentence. Two pages of authorities with one-line verdicts orient no one') and guidance/editorial.md ('Say what the texts say, plainly — Plain is not flat': 'One idea to a sentence... A run of names with one-line verdicts'; 'Write to the reader with gravity and wonder — Read it aloud'). Concrete instances: 12:11 (two consecutive 60-word sentences, the second chaining Bellarmine, Augustine, and Aquinas as three semicolon-strung verdicts), 12:15 (60-word semicolon chain of Chrysostom, Durandus, and Augustine), 12:23 (47-word sentence stacking Gregory, Cyril, Bede, and Augustine followed by a 43-word four-clause Ambrose stack), 12:29 (70-word sentence chaining seven authors—Bellarmine, Sicard, Bernard, Gueranger, Augustine, Schuster, and Durandus—through parentheses and semicolons), 13:15 (94-word sentence), 13:42 (76-word and 86-word sentences back to back), 13:44 (66-word three-part chain), 13:53 (three consecutive 51-77-word sentences), 13:60 (82-word sentence chaining Bellarmine, Rupert, and Schuster), 13:64 (three consecutive 55-68-word sentences), 13:75 (109-word sentence stacking all three interpretations, Durandus, Beleth, Rupert, Bernard, and RGMR 507), and 13:88 (94-word closing sentence).
findings.required_result: Break up the semicolon-chained author stacks and multi-argument sentences across sections/12-concise-themes.tex and sections/13-concise-commentary.tex so that each sentence carries one clear idea and reads naturally aloud, letting sections/12 orient the reader through the Mass's texts and central interpretive divide rather than listing every supporting commentator's one-line verdict before section 13 develops them, while preserving every attribution and qualification. Plain rewrites illustrating the target register: (1) for 12:29, replace the 70-word seven-author chain with: 'At Communion, the choir sings Psalm 84:13 without the opening "For" (Etenim): "The Lord will give goodness: and our earth shall yield her fruit." St. Robert Bellarmine and Sicard of Cremona read that goodness as the Holy Spirit overshadowing the Virgin Mary to bring forth Christ. St. Augustine, whose Old Latin Psalter read "sweetness" (suavitatem), expounds it instead of sinners' hearts ploughed by confession, while Bl. Ildefonso Schuster applies it to Holy Communion refreshing arid souls.' (2) for 12:11, replace the 60-word three-author verdict chain with: 'The psalm's opening cry draws three distinct accents. St. Robert Bellarmine hears a soul tearing itself from earthly "briers and thorns" to trust God alone. St. Augustine hears the whole Christ (totus Christus), Head speaking in His Church, praying against pride. St. Thomas Aquinas, following St. John Damascene, takes lifting the soul as prayer itself: the ascent of the intellect into God (ascensus intellectus in Deum).' (3) for 13:75, split the 109-word sentence into three crisp sentences—one per interpretation—respecting Rupert III.2's actual wording per SYN-001.

findings.problem: The concise study uses unexpanded rubrical abbreviations ('RGMR 507' in reader-facing body prose at 13:75; 'AAS', 'RG', and 'RGMR' at 14:4, 13) without ever defining them anywhere in the standalone concise document, and 14:4 lists rubric numbers (RG 137 for dalmatics/folded chasubles, RGMR 424--425 for Prayers at the Foot of the Altar, and RGMR 500--501 for the Roman Canon) for matters not mentioned in the concise study.
findings.required_result: Spell out Acta Apostolicae Sedis (AAS), Rubricae generales (RG), and Rubricae generales Missalis romani (RGMR) at first use in 14:4, replace bare '(RGMR 507)' in 13:75 with plain prose (keeping the citation in 14:4), and trim rubric numbers in 14:4 to those actually governing items discussed in the concise study.

findings.problem: Three minor presentation and quotation-precision blemishes remain: (1) the comparison table row labeled 'Luke 21:25--30' at 13:81 includes St. Bede and St. Augustine's exposition of Luke 21:33 ('renewal per imaginem'); (2) the row labeled 'Four Senses' at 13:85 lists only Allegorical, Moral, and Anagogical senses without noting the shared Literal sense above; and (3) 12:29 and 13:36 render Dom Prosper Gueranger (The Liturgical Year I, p. 137) as '"our Earth ... made fruitful by the dew of heaven"', splicing across a sentence boundary ('whom our Earth is going to bring forth... This Earth, which is ours, is the Blessed Virgin Mary made fruitful by the dew of heaven').
findings.required_result: Change the row label at 13:81 to 'Luke 21:25--33', clarify the row label or note at 13:85 ('Spiritual Senses' or 'Four Senses (Literal shared above)'), and split the Gueranger quotation at 12:29 and 13:36 into two separate short phrases ('"our Earth"' and '"made fruitful by the dew of heaven"', matching sections/05-lane-incarnational.tex:26).

summary: Independent cold source review of the concise study for liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/01-first-sunday-of-advent (synthesis.tex, sections/10-concise-inventory.tex through sections/14-concise-apparatus.tex, and generated/scriptural-date-location-page.tex). Read the concise study first without consulting the expansive study and independently recovered all three interpretations' distinct exegetical answers (eschatological detachment before the strict Judge, Incarnational and Marian fulfillment at St. Mary Major, and interior conversion with Eucharistic purification between the comings), verified the complete opening semantic sequence and 1962 isolation, and then compared the concise text against the accepted expansive study (sections/01-09), propers/verified.md, research/scope.md, research/interpretations.md, research/source-bindings.toml, and direct primary-witness passages in src/sources/works/ (Gregory Hom. 1, Ambrose Exp. in Luc. X.37-45, Cyril Serm. CXXXIX, Bede on Luke 21:32-33, Augustine Enarr. in Ps. 24 & 84, Sermo 185.1, Confessions VIII.12.29, Chrysostom Hom. 24, Leo Serm. 17.1, Bellarmine on Pss. 24/79/84, Bernard In Adventu 2/3/4/5 and Missus est Hom. 1, Aquinas Postilla on Ps. 24, Schuster I pp. 321-323, Gueranger I p. 137, Durandus VI.2-3, Sicard V.2, Rupert III.2, and Beleth LV & LXIV). Concrete Page-2 lookup on generated/scriptural-date-location-page.tex (research/chronology-table.tex and research/chronology-annotations.tex) succeeded: 'Gospel: Luke 21:25--33' pairs cleanly across two rows with 'Narrated event: Jesus teaches in Jerusalem about the coming of the Son of Man' ('Date unresolved') and 'Composition: The Gospel of St Luke' ('Disputed: c. A.D. 70; Before Acts and the end of Paul's Roman imprisonment'); 'Introit: Ps. 24:1--3 (Vg.; Heb. 25), Ps. 24:4 (Vg.; Heb. 25)' separates 'Traditional attribution: David's reign in the usual chronology; Hebron, then Jerusalem' ('c. 1055--1015 B.C. (usual chronology; Corbett also reports dates 30--50 years later)'), 'Historical setting' ('Occasion date unresolved'), and 'Composition: Psalms' ('Before c. 165 B.C.'), with Vg./Heb. explained once and a pointer to the expansive study (absence of composition/recipient place for Romans, Luke, and Ps. 84 belongs to the shared orientation-v3 projection, not this synthesis). Limit: this dispatch seals canonical TeX sources only, so no compiled PDF or physical pagination was inspected. Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED on three synthesis-owned blocking defects (compression-induced factual and attribution errors across sections/12 and 13, bundled multi-author credits in the Page 1 Four-Sense Overview in sections/11, and a recurring register pattern of semicolon-chained one-line author verdicts and 50-109-word multi-argument sentences across sections/12 and 13), plus two non-blocking advisories.
